recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5454; future UDI work should proceed through current Device/DeviceDefinition UDI issues rather than this merged DSTU1 ballot comment.
issue_request: FHIR-5454 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request from the January 2015 DSTU1 ballot asking whether Device UDI was US-realm-specific and requesting text explaining why UDI belongs in core if it is not universal.
initial_application: No source commit found in current history explicitly names FHIR-5454. The Jira resolution and comments say the comment was merged with FHIR-5505; commit 85cad2a017a228c70b358dab887c56b5bfccb18e pre-applied FHIR-5505 with related Device UDI ballot comments, and commit 966df8c99a9ec454013169646fe4862b168b0b03 later rewrote the Device UDI section around IMDRF, FDA as a US example, other jurisdictions, DI/PI components, and local repositories.
additional_context: FHIR-5505 is already represented on the combined branch by no-change audit commit d7cca4e1f0b5ea99f3986a1eaed82953e17edf57. Device is active in the current build, and later FHIR-5849 reconciliation preserved the jurisdictional/local repository clarification while fixing adjacent UDI scope wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current Device introduction, notes, and udiCarrier definition already explain that UDI is used according to local jurisdictions, cite IMDRF as the base specification, mention other jurisdictions, and allow multiple UDIs for devices sold across jurisdictions.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-5454 was explicitly merged into this Published/Persuasive with Modification Device UDI wording issue, already audited on the combined branch.
Earlier Device UDI harmonization history changed the old UDI representation but is broader than the seed's global-vs-US clarification.
Later Device UDI scope reconciliation changed the same notes while preserving the jurisdictional/local repository clarification relevant to FHIR-5454.
